subject: Endpoint modeling & deployment path qualification — network L3 asks and action plan
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Endpoint modeling & deployment path qualification — network L3 asks and action plan

Hi Eva — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the Private VPC work accurately.

Summary from today's discovery:
- FinBank prefers an isolated path for PII-sensitive model inference (goal: avoid public egress).
- Primary candidate: Private VPC (PrivateLink or VPC peering) vs Dedicated capacity — you leaned toward PrivateLink for per-account isolation.
- Network ops needs: allowlist-able egress, cert/KMS questions, and an internal architecture diagram to confirm routing/NAT behavior.

Immediate asks for sizing and infra recommendations (please attach where helpful):
1) Can you share the internal network diagram and the team-owner we should loop in for firewall/allowlist rules?
2) Do you require PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) specifically, or is VPC peering acceptable if we provide strict route controls?
3) Do you have an existing BYOK / customer-managed KMS requirement for inference keys?
4) Any egress IP constraints (static ranges) we should provide for allowlists?

Attachments: network_req_template.xlsx (fill in subnets, firewall, and contact info).

Plan / next steps we propose:
- You share the network diagram + point-of-contact (Network Ops).
- We provide a PrivateLink vs Peering quick spec (ports, sample routing, TLS/KMS notes).
- Schedule a 45-min network deep-dive with our infra engineer (Aditya) to align on NAT, egress, and certificate flow.

Would Tuesday or Thursday morning next week work for a deep-dive? I looped Marissa for delivery SLAs and technical doc output.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.ai] | +1 415-555-0183

From: Eva Martin <eva@finbank.com>

Date: 2027-07-11T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Endpoint modeling & deployment path qualification — network L3 asks and action plan

Thanks, Jasmine. Good recap. A few immediate notes from our side:

- We do prefer a PrivateLink-style endpoint for isolation; peering is acceptable only if we can avoid transitive routes across prod subnets.
- We can share a network diagram — attaching the current internal high-level diagram for now (finbank-internal-network-diagram.png).
- Egress: finance apps use a handful of static NAT IPs; I need to confirm exact ranges with Network Ops but expect a small set (3-6 IPs).
- KMS: yes, we have a BYOK requirement for anything that holds or wraps keys; security will require details on key lifecycle and HSM usage.

Two quick questions: 
1) For Hosted API, do you have published egress IP ranges we can allowlist for outbound callbacks?
2) If we go Private VPC, what ports/protocols does Redwood expect between our VPC and your PrivateLink endpoint?

I'll get the precise NAT IP list by tomorrow and loop Network Ops for the deep-dive. Prefer Thursday 10:00 AM PT for the network call.

Thanks — Eva
Eva Martin
Head of Cloud Security, FinBank
[eva@finbank.com]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Martin <eva@finbank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-12T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Endpoint modeling & deployment path qualification — network L3 asks and action plan

Eva — appreciate the diagram and the quick replies. Looping Aditya (infra lead) to join the deep-dive. Answers below to your two questions and some extra detail to help Network Ops evaluate.

1) Hosted API egress ranges
- Hosted API (shared) uses a dynamic pool and is NOT suitable for allowlist-only deployments — it is meant for low-friction trials. We can provide a best-effort set of egress ranges for webhooks, but they are not guaranteed stable for production-grade allowlists. For production allowlist needs we recommend Dedicated or Private VPC.

2) Private VPC connectivity (PrivateLink vs VPC Peering)
- PrivateLink (preferred for isolation):
  - Model: RedLink endpoint in your VPC (AWS PrivateLink / GCP Private Service Connect equivalent).
  - Ports: TCP 443 (mutual TLS), outbound from your service to Redwood endpoint. No inbound open ports required.
  - IPs: connection is via ENIs in your account — there are no public egress IPs from our side for traffic to your VPC.
  - Pros: minimal routing changes, strong cross-account isolation, easier to audit.

- VPC Peering option:
  - Model: routable peering between Redwood-managed subnet and your VPC.
  - Considerations: requires careful route table management to avoid transitive routing; you must own the NAT/egress.
  - Ports: TCP 443; additional ports only if you plan to push logs/metrics directly into your collectors (e.g., 443/8443).

3) BYOK / KMS
- Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for data-at-rest encryption in Private deployments. We'll need a short KMS integration checklist (we'll send). For hosted/Dedicated we can discuss HSM-backed options under an enterprise agreement.

4) Sample output for allowlist & preflight (what we'll provide before the call)
- One-page spec: endpoint DNS / expected handshake, port 443 only, mTLS/CA thumbprint where applicable.
- Template for your NAT IPs and subnet blocks for validation (we received your diagram — thanks).
- Next-step: 45-min deep-dive on Thu Jul 15 10:00 AM PT (you indicated availability) — Aditya will cover routing/NAT and Marissa will cover SLA/ops.

Attachments: privatelink-vs-peering-onepager.pdf, network_req_template.xlsx (filled with the fields we'll need).

Aditya / Marissa — please confirm availability for Thu 10:00 AM PT and if you'd like a pre-call alignment.

Best,
Jasmine
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
